rows.ARS:
Dark red Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: Oklahoma (Hybrid Tea, Swim & Weeks, 1963)
Exhibition name: Oklahoma
rows.Origin:
Bred by Swim & Weeks (United States, before 1963).
Introduced in United States by Weeks Wholesale Rose Grower, Inc. in 1964 as 'Oklahoma'.
Introduced by Unknown (Australia) in 1966 as 'Oklahoma'.
rows.Bloom: Dark red. Strong, old rose, sweet fragrance. 45 to 50 petals. Average diameter 5". Large, high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Matte, dark green, leathery foliage.

Height: 4' to 8' (120 to 245cm). Width: up to 4' (up to 120cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b through 10b. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) . Can be grown in the ground or in a container (container requires winter protection).
rows.Patents: United States - Patent No: PP 2,326 on 17 Dec 1963 VIEW USPTO PATENT
rows.Parentage:
Chrysler Imperial (Hybrid Tea, Lammerts, 1952) ×
Charles Mallerin (HT, Meilland, by 1947)
rows.Notes: The State of Oklahoma was admitted to the Union on 16 November 1907.
